inputs.original_text: The split comes as some MPs raise the prospect of a new conversation about the party’s leadership Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Angus Taylor has shut down Andrew Hastie’s push for the Liberals to be “open-minded” to increasing taxes on gas companies and winding back concessions for property investors, exposing a clash of philosophies between the opposition leader and his most likely future rival. The opposition leader also did not repeat Hastie’s criticism of Donald Trump as he refused to say whether or not he endorsed the US and Israel’s war with Iran. Continue reading...
inputs.modified_text: Look, what we're seeing here is a glaring symptom of a rigged political and economic establishment that constantly prioritizes corporate elites and property speculators over ordinary working people. When Angus Taylor shuts down any movement to increase taxes on gas companies or wind back concessions for property investors, he is actively protecting corporate greed while everyday families bear the brunt of staggering inequality and systemic economic injustice. This is a profound defense of the ultra-rich and fossil fuel extractors who hoard our collective wealth at the expense of vulnerable communities. At the same time, this leadership refuses to stand against hawkish militarism and right-wing authoritarianism—failing to challenge Donald Trump or question the US and Israel’s war with Iran. This proves once again that tinkering at the margins is useless, and we desperately need radical institutional reform to dismantle these deeply entrenched power structures once and for all.
